messages:
support_jen: Customer (ACME) reporting frequent tail-latency spikes and occasional 500s on /v1/embeddings. Started ~2026-03-05 14:22 UTC. Symptoms: lots of long-lived requests (~6s+) when overall qps is moderate. They say embedding vector dims look fine.
eng_sam: putting ticket SUP-5891 on this thread. Can you paste a minimal repro + headers? Also their plan: they tried increasing max_concurrency which made it worse.
support_jen: customer sent an SDK snippet and headers. Key parts:
```
POST /v1/embeddings
Authorization: Bearer xxxxx
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "model": "open-embed-1024",
  "inputs": [ ... ~1200 items per request ...],
  "client_batch_preference": {"max_batch_size": 0}
}
```
They said their SDK default set max_batch_size=0 after upgrade to their in-house wrapper.
mike_infra: looking at runtime traces - we see many requests coalesced into enormous batches (2k-3k rows) despite the route configured max_batch_size=512. Looks like server-side validation treated client-supplied 0 as "take whole queue" because of a codepath bug in v1.14 of batcher.
mike_infra: logs (trimmed):
```
[00:14:22] batcher: enqueue req id=abcd size=1 pref_max=0
[00:14:22] batcher: coalesce window=200ms -> merged batch size=2104
[00:14:23] shard-3: start exec batch 2104 tokens  -> exec latency 5600ms
[00:14:28] shard-3: complete exec -> one slow item, others timed out
```
carol: I can repro locally: run this stress script (sends many small requests with pref_max=0). Using python requests in a tight loop.
```
# repro.py
import requests
for i in range(1200):
    requests.post('https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings', json={
      'model':'open-embed-1024', 'inputs':['a']
      ,'client_batch_preference':{'max_batch_size':0}
    }, headers={'Authorization': 'Bearer X'})
```
carol: repro reliably creates one giant batch after coalesce_window fires, causes tail spikes.
eng_sam: Root cause hypothesis: client sets max_batch_size=0 which due to a validation bug is treated as "no limit" instead of clamped to route max (512). Dynamic-batcher coalesces everything in the window -> huge batch -> single shard processing creates stragglers and timeouts. Also priority preemption interacts badly: bulk requests were lower priority and sat until coalesced.
alice_prod: customer also saw billing anomalies since those giant batches consumed tokens faster; they're worried about overage spikes.
support_jen: immediate mitigation options suggested to customer:
- set client_batch_preference.max_batch_size to 512 (or remove it)
- set coalesce_window_ms to 25 for their route (reduces giant coalesces)
- set header X-Redwood-Batch-Max: 512 (temporary server-side override)
- route heavy clients to Dedicated pool

mike_infra: engineering workaround in runtime: enforce route-configured hard cap at enqueue time (patch in review: PR #4521). Also adding a validation rule: treat <=0 as invalid and coerce to configured route max. Backfill: recorded as BUG-RUNTIME-2026-047.
sre-bot: Incident INC-2026-312 opened, linked to SUP-5891, pager duty paged eng-runtime.
eng_sam: PR merged to staging. Plan: roll to prod canary for 10% shards tonight. Patch notes:
```
- enforce hard max_batch_size at enqueue
- clamp client-provided max_batch_size in [1, route_max]
- add metric batcher.client_max_overrides
```
carol: added repro script to the ticket, attached flamegraphs and batch histograms.
support_jen: customer accepted temporary header workaround and reduced their SDK max to 512. They reported immediate improvement in tail-latency (median down, 99th from ~6s to ~250ms).
alice_prod: customer concerned about a billing spike, support provided billing credit talk track and will monitor usage for next 48h.
eng_sam: follow-ups: 1) watch batch size histogram for next 24h 2) add a health check alert on "avg_batch_size > route_max * 1.5" 3) backport patch to previous stable branch.
support_jen: marking as escalated -> resolved when prod rollout completes. Will update SUP-5891 with timeline and customer note. :white_check_mark:
